Variety while preserving the selected level

Compare repetition within the same difficulty, then check length fit and separation between levels. More semantic distance alone is not a quality win: unrelated or unanswerable replies can also be far apart.

Editable screening targets, not validated acceptance criteria. A full 30-response condition is needed to assess all three levels. No combined “quality score.”

Length and complexity separation

The rows are requested difficulty levels. Look for short, mostly non-overlapping word-count bands and a gradual increase in language demands. Word and sentence length are surface proxies, not reliable CEFR scores.

Semantic map — an inspection aid

Each point is one response. Nearby points have similar embedding patterns; inspect them to discover shared situations, subjects or phrasing. Identical responses overlap.

The axes are not difficulty, variety or quality. PCA compresses hundreds of embedding dimensions into two directions. Left/right and up/down have no linguistic labels. A wide-looking cloud is not a winning prompt.

Use the full-dimensional cosine tables to compare diversity. Click or drag on the map to read a cluster, then use “Find similar” for neighbors in the original embedding space.
